messages.subject: Inla keep failing, suddenly
parts:
Dear INLA Development Team,

Greetings!

I am a user of the INLA package and have recently encountered a couple of issues while running some Bayesian statistical models. I am reaching out for your assistance in resolving these problems.

Issue 1: Model Execution Failure

Over the past few days, I have been using the INLA package to run several models. To my confusion, models that were previously successful are now failing to execute. I have tested with the most basic models using minimal covariates (baseline models), but the issue persists. I use the same dataset, same code, and it was still successful 3 hours ago. This issue appear suddenly and I could not solve. The error message I am receiving is as follows:

*** inla.core.safe: The inla program failed, but will rerun in case better initial values may help. try=1/1 For more details using debug=T , verbose=T
> form_i y ~ 1 + offset(logpop) + f(month, model = "rw1", hyper = hyper2.rw, cyclic = TRUE, scale.model = TRUE, constr = TRUE, replicate = cityx) + f(polyid, model = "bym2", graph = nbmatrix_name, replicate = yearx, scale.model = TRUE, constr = TRUE, adjust.for.con.comp = TRUE, hyper = hyper.bym2) > # save storage by cutting all unnecessary variables and only keep specified variable > dd_i <- ddf %>% + dplyr::select( + city, + cityid, + countyid, + county, + year, + month, + total_cases, + logpop, + polyid, + yearx, + cityx, + areaidx, + urban_log, + transportation_log, + out_migration_g, + Cropland_log, + Forest_log, + elevation_log + ) %>% + dplyr::mutate(y = total_cases) %>% + cbind(ddf[ , grep(as.vector(fx_i$fx), names(ddf)), drop=FALSE]) > # fit model > mod_i = tryCatch( + fitINLAModel(form_i, dd_i, family="nbinomial", verbose=TRUE), + error = function(e) return(e) + ) [1] "head(scale)" NULL [1] "head(weights)" NULL [1] "head(Ntrials)" NULL [1] "head(offset)" NULL [1] "head(E)" NULL [1] "head(strata)" NULL [1] "head(lp.scale)" NULL [1] "head(link.covariates)" NULL [1] "MPredictor 0" [1] "NPredictor 8892" [1] "NData 8892" [1] "y...fake has length 8892" n.family 1 [1] "Entries with same length:" "city" "cityid" [4] "countyid" "county" "year" [7] "month" "total_cases" "logpop" [10] "polyid" "yearx" "cityx" [13] "areaidx" "urban_log" "transportation_log" [16] "out_migration_g" "Cropland_log" "Forest_log" [19] "elevation_log" "y...fake" *** inla.core.safe: The inla program failed, but will rerun in case better initial values may help. try=1/1 [1] "MPredictor 0" [1] "NPredictor 8892" [1] "NData 8892" [1] "y...fake has length 8892" n.family 1 [1] "Entries with same length:" "city" "cityid" [4] "countyid" "county" "year" [7] "month" "total_cases" "logpop" [10] "polyid" "yearx" "cityx" [13] "areaidx" "urban_log" "transportation_log" [16] "out_migration_g" "Cropland_log" "Forest_log" [19] "elevation_log" "y...fake"

And this is the function I used to run Inla:
fitINLAModel = function(formx, data, family, config=FALSE, verbose=TRUE, return.marginals=FALSE){
 
  return(
   
    INLA::inla(
     
      # formula, data and model family
      formx,
      data = data,
      family = family,
      safe = TRUE,  # enable possible restarts to improve initial values and Hessian if needed
      # fixed effects calibration
      control.fixed = list(mean.intercept=0,
                           prec.intercept=1, # precision 1
                           mean=0,
                           prec=1), # weakly regularising on fixed effects (sd of 1)
     
      # save predicted values on response scale
      control.predictor = list(compute=FALSE,
                               link=1),
     
      # items to compute
      control.compute = list(cpo=TRUE,
                             waic=TRUE,
                             dic=TRUE,
                             config=config, # set config to TRUE if want to do INLA::inla.posterior.sample()
                             return.marginals=return.marginals), # do not return marginals unless specified (saves memory)
     
      # configure inla approx
      control.inla = control.inla(strategy = "auto"),                    
      # verbose?
      inla.mode = "experimental", # new version of INLA algorithm (requires R 4.1 and INLA testing version)
      verbose = verbose,
      debug=T
    )
  )
 
}


Issue 2: Execution Issues with Complex Models

Assuming Issue 1 can be resolved, I would also like to inquire about handling errors when running more complex models. In my previous experience, I have noticed that adding certain covariates to the model allows it to run successfully, but introducing additional covariates sometimes causes the model to fail. Are there any general strategies or best practices you could share for dealing with this kind of situation?

I am willing to provide the relevant data and code snippets, which can be sent as attachments or through any other method you prefer.

Thank you for your time and assistance. I am looking forward to your response and hope to resolve these issues promptly to continue with my research work.

Best regards

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Inla keep failing, suddenly
parts:
Make sure your using R 4.4 (4.3 is also ok) and rerun on the most recent testing version of INLA, with options verbose=T,debug=T 


If that does not work well, please share data code so we can check here 

—
Haavard Rue
Helpdesk
he...@r-inla.org
